intro: When you search for a clinical negligence solicitor near me, you are likely dealing with the aftermath of medical treatment that went wrong and caused harm to you or someone close to you. You want to know your options and find a solicitor who can handle a claim sensitively and locally. We can introduce you to a suitable UK solicitor who will quote you directly for your case.
need_heading: What people searching for a clinical negligence solicitor usually need
need_lead: People in this situation often need clear guidance on whether they have a claim and how to pursue it without adding to their stress.
needs: You want to understand if the care you received fell below an acceptable standard and whether that caused you harm.
You need help gathering medical records and expert evidence to support your claim.
You are concerned about the cost and want to know if no win, no fee arrangements are available.
You may be approaching the three-year time limit for starting a claim and need urgent advice.
You would prefer to speak with a solicitor near you who can meet in person or who understands local services.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about clinical negligence claims
context: Clinical negligence claims usually must be started within three years of the harm occurring, or of the date you became aware of it, so time is important. Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, solicitors are regulated by the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland by the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

Many clinical negligence solicitors work on no win, no fee terms, which means you may not have to pay upfront. It is also worth checking that the person handling your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive (CILEx) or another authorised professional, because the word 'lawyer' is not protected on its own. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure; if that does not resolve things, the Legal Ombudsman can look at service complaints in England and Wales.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe briefly what happened, including the type of medical treatment and when it took place.
Explain what harm you believe was caused and how it has affected you.
Mention whether you have already obtained any medical records or reports.
State whether you are enquiring for yourself or on behalf of someone else.
Indicate if you have spoken to other solicitors or if any claim has already been started.
Include your location and whether you need to meet the solicitor in person.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the clinical negligence solicitor
questions: What experience do you have with claims involving my type of medical treatment?
How will you assess whether I have a claim and what evidence will you need?
Will you work on a no win, no fee basis, and what costs might I be responsible for?
How long do you expect the claim to take, and what are the key stages?
Who will handle my case day to day, and are they a solicitor or other authorised professional?
What is your approach to communication and keeping me updated?

faqs.q: How long do I have to make a clinical negligence claim?
faqs.a: In most cases, you must start a claim within three years of the harm occurring or of the date you became aware of it. There are exceptions, so it is best to seek advice promptly.

faqs.q: Will I have to pay upfront for a clinical negligence solicitor?
faqs.a: Many clinical negligence solicitors work on no win, no fee terms, so you may not need to pay upfront. However, you should always ask about any potential costs and disbursements.

faqs.q: What evidence is needed to support a clinical negligence claim?
faqs.a: Medical records and expert evidence are usually key to showing that the care fell below an acceptable standard and caused harm. Your solicitor will help you gather these.

faqs.q: How can I check that a solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

extra_heading: What to expect at your first meeting with a clinical negligence solicitor
extra: At your first meeting, the solicitor will ask you to describe what happened in your own words, from the treatment you received to the harm you believe it caused. They will also want to know when you first became aware that something might have gone wrong, because the three-year time limit for starting a claim usually runs from that date or from the date of the harm itself. This is not a formal interview; it is a chance for you to explain your situation and for the solicitor to understand whether you may have a claim.

The solicitor will then explain how they would investigate your case, which will typically involve obtaining your medical records and instructing independent medical experts to comment on the standard of care. They will discuss funding options with you, including whether they can offer a no win, no fee arrangement, and what costs you might be responsible for even under such an arrangement. You should feel free to ask questions about anything that is unclear, and to take your time before deciding whether to proceed.

It is also worth asking the solicitor about their experience with cases involving the type of medical treatment you received, as clinical negligence covers a very wide range of situations. You may want to know who will handle your case day to day, whether that person is a solicitor or another authorised professional, and how often you will be updated. A good first meeting should leave you feeling informed about your options and under no pressure to commit immediately.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to my first meeting with a clinical negligence solicitor?
extra_faqs.a: It helps to bring any relevant documents you already have, such as correspondence with the hospital or clinic, and a written timeline of events if you can prepare one. You do not need to have everything organised; the solicitor will guide you through what is needed.

extra_faqs.q: Will I have to pay for the first meeting?
extra_faqs.a: Many clinical negligence solicitors offer a free initial consultation, but this is not universal, so it is best to ask when you make the appointment. Any fees for the first meeting should be explained to you clearly beforehand.

extra_faqs.q: Can I bring someone with me to the first meeting?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, you are usually welcome to bring a friend or family member for support, especially if the subject matter is distressing. It can also help to have someone else listen and take notes.
